name: When should kitchen drywall be patched versus replaced completely?

mainEntity.name: When should kitchen drywall be patched versus replaced completely?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should repair minor drywall dents, hairline settle cracks, and surface punctures. However, you should replace the drywall sheets entirely if there is persistent moisture damage, widespread mold growth, or structural crumbling behind sinks and dishwashers. Kitchen walls house major supply lines and drain stacks; if a hidden leak has softened the gypsum core, patching over it only masks deeper trouble. Full replacement allows the contractor to inspect framing, let damp cavities dry out, and ensure plumbing is intact before installing fresh moisture-resistant panels.
acceptedAnswer.description: Patch small holes and surface cracks, but replace drywall entirely if water exposure, plumbing leaks, or mold have softened the gypsum core behind cabinets or appliances.
